findings.title: Session-less requests are served as a global "dashboard Teacher" actor; unauthenticated GET returns cross-school support tickets
findings.evidence: `lib/iam.js:199-210` falls back to `getDashboardRoleUser()` when there is no session; `lib/currentUser.js:9` keeps the role in `globalThis.__CURRENT_USER__`; every web login calls `setCurrentRole` (`app/actions/auth.js:92,111,138`), so the last web Teacher login makes every cookie-less request a Teacher. That fallback actor has no `schoolId`. Live, no cookie: `GET /api/iam/me` returned a Teacher user, `/api/exams`, `/api/classes/sections-map`, `/api/subjects`, `/api/notices` returned 200, and `GET /api/support/tickets` returned ticket objects (including `ticketNumber`, `schoolId`) because `getSchoolTickets(undefined)` (`lib/support.js` where `{schoolId: undefined}`) applies no filter, i.e. tickets of ALL schools (`app/api/support/tickets/route.js`, `lib/support.js getSchoolTickets`).
findings.impact: unauthenticated cross-tenant read of support tickets (subjects, messages, names, attachment URLs); unauthenticated access to every route that only checks `if (!actor)`. State depends on which role last logged in on that server instance, so it is intermittent in serverless but permanent on a long-lived instance.
findings.recommendation: remove the dashboard-toggle branch from `getCurrentUserInfo` (return `null` when `getSession()` is empty); delete `lib/currentUser.js` global state or confine it to a dev flag; in `getSchoolTickets` and similar helpers throw if `schoolId` is falsy.

findings.title: POST /api/schools has no authentication and repoints the global active-school singleton
findings.evidence: `app/api/schools/route.js:21-53` — no `requireSuperAdmin` (only the `GET` at line 7 has it). It calls `addSchoolFromWizard` (`lib/schools.js:120`, creates a School), then `setActiveSchoolContext(school)` (`lib/school.js`, mutates `globalThis.__ACTIVE_SCHOOL__`) and `addSession`/`setActiveSession`.
findings.impact: anyone can create tenants (code collision probing, junk rows) and repoint the instance's fallback school, which affects the cron job, SuperAdmin sessions and API-001 actors for all later requests on that instance.
findings.recommendation: `const { error } = await requireSuperAdmin(); if (error) return error;` at the top; pass the new school id explicitly to session creation instead of mutating the singleton.

findings.title: Five handlers have no auth check on any path (fee ledger, create-order, verify, attendance by student, subjects GET)
findings.evidence: ledger `route.js:5-18` only blocks a Parent for a different child, never 401s on null; `create-order/route.js:11-17` and `verify/route.js:11-17` run the ownership check only when `actor?.role === 'Parent'`, otherwise proceed; `attendance/student/[id]/route.js:20-22` same pattern; `subjects/route.js:11`. Contrast the sibling `fees/student/[studentId]/route.js` which was fixed.
findings.impact: payment history and attendance of any student readable without login; unauthenticated Razorpay order creation (creates PENDING Payment rows and live Razorpay orders: abuse/spam); unauthenticated verify.
findings.recommendation: use `requireParent`/`requirePermission('fees.view')` or at minimum `if (!actor) 401` plus ownership check for any non-admin role; add a shared `requireActor()` helper.

findings.title: Roles/permissions are global (not per tenant); any holder of permissions.manage edits roles for all schools
findings.evidence: `prisma Role` has `key @unique` and no `schoolId` (`schema.prisma:70-82`); `app/api/roles/[id]/permissions/route.js` replaces `RolePermission` rows of that single global role; `prisma/rbacPermissions.js:98` gives `PRINCIPAL = ALL_KEYS` which includes `permissions.manage` (`:70`).
findings.impact: a Principal of school A can change what Admin/Teacher/Accountant may do in every other school (including granting themselves nothing more, but revoking fees access platform-wide, or giving Teachers `students.delete`).
findings.recommendation: restrict `permissions.manage` to SuperAdmin, or make roles per-school. **Effort:** S (restrict) / L (per-school)

findings.title: Student documents (birth cert, Aadhaar, SLC) uploaded to a public-read R2 prefix with predictable keys
findings.evidence: `lib/storage.js:20-26` (public URL, comment requires public-read bucket); `app/api/students/document-upload-url/route.js:28` key = `students/<schoolId>/documents/<Date.now()>-<safeName>`; `app/api/support/upload-url/route.js:33` same pattern; `route.js:19-25` size/type trusted from the client.
findings.impact: identity documents of minors/parents are readable by anyone who obtains or guesses the URL (millisecond timestamp plus a usually predictable filename such as `aadhaar.pdf`); the URL is persisted and returned to every client that renders the student. No access revocation or audit is possible; deleting a student does not necessarily delete the object. This is a privacy/regulatory exposure (India's DPDP Act for children's data).
findings.recommendation: minimum: add `crypto.randomUUID()` to every key. Better: keep sensitive prefixes (`students/*/documents/`, Aadhaar) in a private bucket and serve through an authenticated route that returns a short-lived presigned GET (`@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` is already installed). Also pass `ContentLength` via a presigned POST policy or re-check the object size with `HeadObject` on confirm.

findings.title: Fee-generation cron processes one school only (global singleton), and fails open if CRON_SECRET is unset
findings.evidence: `lib/fees.js:583-607` `generateDueStudentFees` calls `getFeeStructures()` which resolves the school via `resolveSchoolId()` (`lib/fees.js:217`) with no session, i.e. the global singleton (`lib/school.js`, defaults to a seed id). `app/api/cron/generate-fees/route.js:12-15` and `cleanup-support-tickets/route.js` only check the bearer when `process.env.CRON_SECRET` is set (fail-open).
findings.impact: in a multi-school deployment only one school gets auto-generated fees; the rest silently never do. If the secret is missing the endpoints are publicly callable (mass generation / ticket purge).
findings.recommendation: loop `prisma.school.findMany({status:'Active'})` and pass `schoolId` into every lib call; return 500 when `CRON_SECRET` is unset.

findings.title: No Razorpay webhook; verification relies on the browser callback; abandoned checkouts lose captured payments
findings.evidence: no `webhook` route exists under `app/api`; `lib/fees.js:1186-1193` comment acknowledges it. `verifyRazorpayPayment` (`lib/fees.js:1194-1265`) is reached only from the client POST.
findings.impact: if the parent's browser/app closes, loses network, or the callback fails after Razorpay captures money, the Payment row stays PENDING forever (no cleanup job, comment at `lib/fees.js:1142`) and the fee stays unpaid: money taken, school sees no payment. No reconciliation job either.
findings.recommendation: add `app/api/payments/razorpay/webhook/route.js` verifying `X-Razorpay-Signature` over the raw body with the school's webhook secret, resolving the Payment by `razorpayOrderId`, and reusing one shared `applySuccessfulPayment(paymentId)` that is idempotent and runs in a transaction with a conditional update (`updateMany where status:'PENDING'`).

findings.title: Online/manual payment races and overpayment: stale read, absolute write, many PENDING orders per fee, no cap
findings.evidence: `collectManualPayment` (`lib/fees.js:1025-1081`) reads the fee, computes `newPaidAmount = fee.paidAmount + collectAmount` in JS and writes it as an absolute value; no row lock, no idempotency key. `verifyRazorpayPayment` (`fees.js:1239-1251`) does the same with `payment.amount`, never re-checking that the amount is still owed. `createRazorpayOrder` (`fees.js:1147`) creates a new PENDING order on every call with no reuse or cap.
findings.impact: (1) two concurrent manual collections both pass the `<= remainingDue` check, create two Payment rows, but `paidAmount` is overwritten with one value (ledger sum greater than `paidAmount`); (2) a parent who opened two checkouts, or paid online after an admin collected cash, can have both verified: `paidAmount` exceeds payable, status PAID, no refund path (BIZ-005); (3) double-click on collect creates duplicate Payments.
findings.recommendation: use atomic updates: `prisma.studentFee.updateMany({ where: {id, schoolId, paidAmount: fee.paidAmount}, data:{ paidAmount: {increment: amt}}})` inside the transaction and abort on `count===0`; in verify re-compute remaining due and reject/flag overpay; reuse an existing PENDING order for the same fee; accept an `Idempotency-Key` on `/api/fees/collect`.

findings.title: Attendance lock rules are disabled in code; markedBy and records are client-controlled
findings.evidence: `lib/attendance.js:103-110` `ATTENDANCE_LOCK_ENABLED = false` makes `computeAttendanceAccess` always allow; the manual unlock (`manuallyUnlocked`, `attendance/[id]/lock`) therefore has no effect. `app/api/attendance/route.js` passes the raw body to `saveAttendance` (`lib/attendance.js:57`), which upserts `markedBy` (client supplied, `DailyAttendanceBoard.jsx:202`) and `records` (no schema check: statuses, studentIds belonging to the class, duplicates). Only Sunday is rejected; school calendar holidays and future dates are accepted.
findings.impact: a Teacher can alter any past or future date for their class, forge `markedBy`, and write arbitrary JSON into `records`, corrupting reports. Concurrent submissions are last-write-wins via the `[school, session, date, class, section]` unique upsert (no duplicate rows, which is good).
findings.recommendation: turn the flag on (or delete the dead matrix and decide the policy), derive `markedBy` from the session, validate `records` against the roster and `ATTENDANCE_STATUSES`, reject future dates.

findings.title: Migration history does not represent the schema (1 init migration, 2 of 52 models)
findings.evidence: `prisma/migrations/20260830172048_init/migration.sql:1-38` creates only the `AdminStatus` enum and the `SuperAdmin` and `SchoolAdmin` tables; `prisma/schema.prisma` defines 52 models. `git log -- prisma/migrations` shows only the initial commit. `_prisma_migrations` in the local DB has exactly one row. `package.json:7` build script is `prisma generate && next build` (no `prisma migrate deploy`). The schema header comments and the existence of RBAC/support/enrollment tables in the local DB prove the schema was applied some other way (`db push` style).
findings.impact: A new environment (staging, DR restore target, a second region) cannot be created from the repo; `prisma migrate deploy` would produce a database missing 50 tables. No reviewable, reversible record of schema change; no safe path for additive changes with data (e.g. converting date strings to DateTime). Production schema drift cannot be detected.
findings.recommendation: Baseline: generate a full-schema migration from the production-equivalent schema (`prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script`), mark it applied on existing databases with `prisma migrate resolve --applied`, and from then on use `migrate dev`/`migrate deploy` in the release process.

findings.title: Manual fee collection is a read-modify-write outside the transaction: double-collect / overpay race
findings.evidence: `lib/fees.js:1025-1058` (`collectManualPayment`): reads the fee with `getStudentFeeById`, checks `status === 'PAID'` and `remainingDue` in JS, computes `newPaidAmount = fee.paidAmount + collectAmount`, then runs `$transaction([payment.create, studentFee.update({ paidAmount: newPaidAmount })])`. The transaction does not re-read or lock the fee, and `paidAmount` is written as an absolute value. `lib/fees.js:1194-1250` (`verifyRazorpayPayment`) has the same shape (`fee.paidAmount + payment.amount`). There is no unique key or CHECK constraint tying `sum(Payment.amount where SUCCESS)` to `StudentFee.paidAmount` or capping it at the payable amount (schema `StudentFee`, `Payment`, lines 537-557 and 1427-1443).
findings.impact: Two accountants (or a double click, or a manual collect racing a pending Razorpay verify for the same fee) both pass the "not PAID" check; two SUCCESS Payment rows are created while `paidAmount` reflects only one (or a Razorpay verify adds on top of a manual full payment). Ledger and fee row then disagree; the school's reconciliation breaks and parents can be double-charged. Local DB: fee rows are currently consistent (0 overpaid), so this is a latent defect, not observed corruption.
findings.recommendation: Inside one interactive transaction do the guarded update: `updateMany({ where: { id, schoolId, paidAmount: fee.paidAmount }, data: { paidAmount: { increment: amount }, status } })` and abort if `count === 0`; or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` via `$queryRaw`. For Razorpay mark the pending Payment SUCCESS with `updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'PENDING' } })` first and only continue if it matched.

findings.title: Login identity is looked up by email only, but uniqueness is per school (or absent): ambiguous account resolution
findings.evidence: Schema: `Teacher` has no unique on `loginEmail` or `email` (only `@@unique([schoolId, employeeId])`, `schema.prisma:678`); `ParentAccount` is `@@unique([schoolId, email])` (285); `User` is `@@unique([schoolId, email])` (153); `SchoolAdmin.email` is globally unique (322-326). Lookups: `lib/teachers.js:436-440` and `:460-463` `findFirst({ where: { loginEmail: ... } })` with no school; `lib/parentAccounts.js:108-111` `findFirst` by email only; `lib/rbac.js:44-49` `user.findFirst` by email for Principal/Accountant. Local DB: one group of 4 teachers in one school shares the same `loginEmail` (demo data), 13 of 26 teachers have login enabled.
findings.impact: Two schools can legitimately register the same parent or teacher email (the schema permits it), after which `findFirst` returns an arbitrary row: the person logs into the wrong tenant, or a correct password for school B fails because school A's row was returned first (a person who is a parent at two schools cannot sign in to one). Within a school, duplicate teacher login emails make password-reset and login nondeterministic. This is both an integrity and a tenant-isolation risk (credential of one tenant matched against another tenant's account when passwords coincide).
findings.recommendation: Decide the product rule. Simplest consistent option: login emails are globally unique across tenants (unique index on lowercased email per identity table, or a single `User` identity table), with a data-cleanup migration first. Alternative: require a school code at login and look up `{ schoolId, email }`. Add `@@unique([schoolId, loginEmail])` to Teacher at minimum.

findings.title: Online-payment finalisation depends only on browser callback; no Razorpay webhook
findings.evidence: components/fees/RazorpayPayButton.jsx:63-80; no webhook route under app/api
findings.impact: Captured payments can remain unrecorded if verify call fails; parent may pay twice
findings.recommendation: Add signature-verified idempotent webhook; recovery message on verify failure

findings.title: Demo credentials hard-coded and displayed in production login
findings.evidence: LoginScreen.js:48-58,75,117-118,263 not gated by __DEV__
findings.impact: Release builds expose seeded account credentials; access if accounts exist in production
findings.recommendation: Gate with __DEV__, delete/rotate seeded accounts in production

findings.title: Daily fee-generation cron only processes one fallback school, not every school
findings.evidence: `generateDueStudentFees()` calls `getFeeStructures()` (no school argument); that resolves school through `resolveSchoolId()`, which with no session (a cron has none — the function's own comment at `fees.js:579-583` says so) returns the process-wide `getActiveSchoolId()` singleton (`schoolContext.js:26`, default seed id at `lib/school.js:5,17`).
findings.impact: On a multi-school deployment the daily job generates term fees for at most one school (whichever the instance last "stepped into", else the seed id); all others are silently skipped while the route returns `success: true`. Parents of other schools are not billed on time; no one is alerted.
findings.recommendation: In the cron, `const schools = await prisma.school.findMany({select:{id:true}})` and call a school-parameterised generator for each, collecting per-school success/failure in the response.

findings.title: No Razorpay webhook or reconciliation; paid-but-unrecorded payments possible
findings.evidence: only `create-order` and `verify` routes exist under `app/api/payments/` (directory listing); `lib/fees.js:1191,1257` comments say a webhook is a future addition ("once built"). Payment rows start `PENDING` (`schema.prisma:1437`) and become `SUCCESS` only when the browser/app calls `verify` (`fees.js:1236-1248`). No job re-queries Razorpay for stale `PENDING` rows, and no admin screen lists them. Also `create-order/route.js:13` and `verify/route.js:12` skip the ownership check when no actor is signed in.
findings.impact: If a parent pays and the app/tab closes, the network drops, or the callback fails, money is captured at Razorpay but the fee stays unpaid and the Payment stays `PENDING` indefinitely; staff must reconcile manually against the Razorpay dashboard. Refunds do not exist either (prior audit P28). The null-actor path lets an unauthenticated caller create orders/PENDING rows against any fee id (signature check still protects `verify`).
findings.recommendation: Add `POST /api/payments/razorpay/webhook` (verify `X-Razorpay-Signature` with the webhook secret over the raw body; call the existing idempotent confirm path which already tolerates duplicates, `fees.js:1256-1262`), plus a daily/admin "stale PENDING payments" check that fetches the order status. Require a signed-in actor on `create-order`/`verify`.

findings.title: No CI/CD gates in either repo
findings.evidence: no .github directory in ADMIN or MOBILE; package.json:5-11
findings.impact: Broken or insecure code deploys unchecked; about 100 uncommitted modified files obscure release provenance.
findings.recommendation: GitHub Actions: npm ci, lint, prisma validate, next build with dummy env, tests; protect main.

findings.title: Parent and Accountant roles can read any student's full record (Aadhaar, guardians, address)
findings.evidence: `app/api/students/[id]/route.js:7-19` — gate is `requirePermission('students.view')` followed by a block that rejects only `user.roleKey === 'Teacher'`; the comment (lines 10-16) states the route is meant to be "admin-tier only". `prisma/rbacPermissions.js` grants `students.view` to Parent (line ~205) and Accountant (line 195) as well as Teacher/Admin. `lib/students.js:310-312` returns the full decorated record by `{id, schoolId}`, i.e. including `aadhaarNumber`, guardian/secondary guardian (phones, emails, Aadhaar), address, documents URLs (schema `Student` 372-405).
findings.impact: A signed-in parent can fetch any other student in the same school (ids are cuids, but they are exposed in rosters, notices, links) and read minors' Aadhaar numbers, guardian contacts and addresses. Accountant (no teaching/admin need) gets the same. Same-school only; no cross-tenant leak.
findings.recommendation: In the route, allow only roles that legitimately need the full record: `if (!['Admin','Principal','SuperAdmin'].includes(user.roleKey)) return 403`; Parent already has dedicated parent routes. Consider returning a reduced projection for Accountant.

findings.title: Aadhaar and identity documents stored under permanent unsigned public URLs
findings.evidence: `lib/storage.js:20-27` — `buildPublicUrl` returns `${R2_PUBLIC_URL}/${key}` and its comment states the bucket must allow public reads; there is no signed-GET path in the file. Student document keys are `students/<schoolId>/documents/<Date.now()>-<sanitised original filename>` (`students/document-upload-url/route.js:26-28`); teacher equivalent `teachers/document-upload-url/route.js:22-24`. The URL is stored in the DB (`Student.aadhaarDocumentUrl` schema 383, Teacher 629) and returned to API callers (see PRV-001).
findings.impact: Anyone holding or guessing a URL can download a child's or teacher's Aadhaar/birth-certificate scan with no authentication, no expiry and no access log. Keys are not high-entropy (millisecond timestamp plus a user-chosen filename such as the document type), and URLs leak through any log, referrer, shared screenshot or the PRV-001 route.
findings.recommendation: Smallest change: keep photos public, but store identity documents under a separate private bucket (no public domain) with a random key (`crypto.randomUUID()`), and serve them via a permission-checked route that returns a short-lived presigned GET (`GetObjectCommand` + `getSignedUrl`, 60-300 s). Existing objects need migration.

findings.title: Any signed-in Parent (and Accountant) can write homework and exam marks: routes only require a non-null actor and libs treat every non-Teacher as admin
findings.evidence: lib/examMarks.js:32-33,164-169,243-247; lib/homework.js:201-203,231-232,269-281; app/api/homework/route.js:21-47; app/api/exams/schedules/[scheduleId]/marks/route.js:33-52; app/api/homework/[id]/route.js:5-28 (code-based, not executed)
findings.impact: A parent token (mobile login) can POST/PUT/DELETE homework for any class (with push fan-out to students), read a full class marks sheet and upsert marks for any studentId. Academic-record integrity and spam of every parent in the school.
findings.recommendation: Replace the "role !== Teacher => allow" shortcut with explicit allow-lists (SchoolAdmin/SuperAdmin) and add requirePermission (marks.enter/marks.update, homework manage) at the route; add a negative test per role.

findings.title: Dashboard server pages have no server-side role/permission guard: a signed-in Teacher can render Teachers, Fees, Settings and Promote pages with SSR data
findings.evidence: app/dashboard/teachers/[id]/page.jsx:15-18; app/dashboard/teachers/page.jsx:14-18; app/dashboard/fees/payments/page.jsx:9; app/dashboard/fees/students/page.jsx:15-31; app/dashboard/layout.jsx:10-17; middleware.js:26-30,86-94 (middleware only checks role tier). Not executed.
findings.impact: Hidden sidebar links are the only barrier: typing the URL returns data fetched directly from lib (bypassing API requirePermission), including teacher HR/financial fields (PRV-003) and school-wide fee payments.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared page guard (requirePermission-equivalent for pages) to every dashboard page, or one in app/dashboard/layout per route segment; verify live per role.

findings.title: Process-global tenant and role singletons are mutated by every school-admin/teacher login, so SuperAdmin and session-less requests act on whichever school logged in last
findings.evidence: app/actions/auth.js:76-77,92,100-101,111,138; lib/school.js:29-31,43-45; lib/auth/schoolContext.js:23-27; app/api/schools/[id]/manage/route.js:21-24
findings.impact: SuperAdmin sessions carry no schoolId, so resolveSchoolId() returns the global singleton: a SuperAdmin who stepped into school A can have reads and writes land in school B after a school-B admin logs in. Cross-tenant misdirected writes and disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Remove active-school and dashboard-role singletons; carry the managed schoolId inside the SuperAdmin token or a per-request header validated server-side; resolveSchoolId must throw when no schoolId.

findings.title: next 16.3.2 is in the affected range of critical and high advisories (image optimisation RCE/SSRF, next/og RCE, cache poisoning)
findings.evidence: package.json:24 (next 16.3.2 pinned); npm audit --json: next critical, fix 16.4.1 (non-major). App imports next/image in components/LoginForm.jsx and uses no next/og; exploitability depends on image config and hosting (not verified).

findings.title: API-001 fallback actor also reaches write paths: support ticket replies/reads are unscoped when actor.schoolId is undefined; marks and homework run as the toggle Teacher
findings.evidence: lib/iam.js:197-210; lib/support.js:63-65,110-112,155-158 (undefined schoolId drops the where filter in Prisma); app/api/support/tickets/[id]/replies/route.js:5-19; app/api/support/tickets/[id]/route.js:13 (code-based; dev server not running so not re-tested live)
findings.impact: Beyond the read leak in API-001: a session-less caller can read any ticket by id, list all tenants' tickets and post replies into any tenant's thread (triggering notifications), when a Teacher web login previously ran on that instance.

findings.title: No automated tests in ADMIN (no runner, no test script)
findings.evidence: package.json:5-11 no test script; package.json:13-45 no test framework

findings.title: No server-side schema validation; client-only zod; malformed JSON gives 500
findings.evidence: `lib/schemas.js` (zod, 659 lines) is imported only by client components (e.g. `components/fees/CollectFeeModal.jsx`); no `app/api` route imports it. 110 `await request.json()` calls, 0 with `.catch`; 36 route files have no `try` at all, and in most others `request.json()` sits before the `try`. Validation is `if (!field)` checks. Content-Type is not checked. Mass assignment is limited: `buildStudentFields`/`fieldsFrom` whitelist fields (no raw body spread into prisma found; only server-built `...data` in `examMarks.js:255`, `examSchedules.js:227`).
findings.impact: bad bodies return 500 with a stack in logs; numeric fields (`amount`, `marksObtained`, `maxMarks`) can be strings, NaN, fractional or negative until a lib check catches them.
findings.recommendation: a 10-line `parseBody(request, schema)` helper using the existing zod schemas (reuse `feeStructureSchema`, `manualPaymentSchema`, etc.) returning 400. **Effort:** M

findings.title: Unbounded list responses and unbounded request arrays
findings.evidence: `GET /api/students` returns the full decorated school (`app/api/students/route.js`), for Teachers it loads all students then filters in JS; `GET /api/users`, `GET /api/notices`, `GET /api/homework`, `GET /api/support/tickets`, `GET /api/subjects`, `getPaymentLedger`; `POST bulk-collect` `studentIds`, `students/bulk-import` `rows`, `exams/schedules/.../marks` `rows` and `fees/send-reminder` `studentIds` have no length cap. Paged variants exist for students, teachers, notices, homework, payments (page size capped at 50/100), but `payments` and `schools` do not cap `pageSize`.
findings.recommendation: cap array lengths (e.g. 500) and `pageSize`; migrate remaining list consumers to the paged routes. **Effort:** S–M

findings.title: Upload presign does not bind size; free-form attachmentUrl/photoUrl stored; cleanup cron can delete another tenant's R2 object
findings.evidence: 13 `*upload-url` routes (list: students photo/document, teachers photo/document, school logo, admin/parent/teacher profile photo, notices, support). All require auth and allow-list `fileType`; keys are prefixed by `schoolId` (profile photos by user id) plus a sanitized name. But size is a client-stated `fileSize` only; `getPresignedUploadUrl` (`lib/storage.js`) signs `ContentType` but no `ContentLength`/size condition, so the real size is unlimited; no virus or magic-byte check; URLs are public (`R2_PUBLIC_URL`). `attachmentUrl` (support tickets/replies, `lib/support.js:111,130`) and `photoUrl` (self-profile PATCH) are stored without checking they point to this tenant's key prefix; `cleanupOldTickets` (`lib/support.js:229-232`) deletes whatever R2 key such a URL maps to.
findings.impact: storage abuse; a school user can reference another school's R2 object in a ticket and have it deleted by the cron after 90 days; arbitrary external URL rendered as a link.
findings.recommendation: validate `attachmentUrl`/`photoUrl` start with `R2_PUBLIC_URL + '/<prefix>/<schoolId>/'`; use a presigned POST with `content-length-range`. **Effort:** S–M

findings.title: Rate limiting exists only on logins and is in-memory per instance
findings.evidence: `lib/auth/loginRateLimit.js` is an in-memory `Map` (per instance, reset on cold start), used by login/reset routes only. No limit on create-order, upload-url, support tickets, bulk endpoints, or fee collection.
findings.recommendation: a shared store (Upstash/Postgres) for login; per-user caps on order creation and ticket creation. **Effort:** M

findings.title: No Razorpay webhook: payment recording depends on the browser returning to the verify endpoint
findings.evidence: `app/api/payments/razorpay/` contains only `create-order/route.js` and `verify/route.js`; `lib/fees.js:1194-1265` `verifyRazorpayPayment` is idempotent (SUCCESS short-circuit at ~1214, unique `razorpayPaymentId` P2002 handling at ~1257-1262) but only runs when the client calls it; the comment at 1257 anticipates a webhook "once built".
findings.impact: if a parent pays and the app/browser dies, loses network, or the tab closes before `verify`, Razorpay captured the money while the `Payment` row stays `PENDING` and the fee stays unpaid. Schools see disputes and manual reconciliation. Double-submit safety is good; lost-callback safety is absent.
findings.recommendation: add `app/api/payments/razorpay/webhook/route.js` (raw body, `X-Razorpay-Signature` HMAC with a per-school webhook secret, handle `payment.captured`/`order.paid`), reusing the existing idempotent finalize logic from `verifyRazorpayPayment`. Add a nightly reconcile of PENDING payments older than 30 min via Razorpay `orders.fetchPayments`.

findings.title: No refund/reversal path; no collector or actor recorded on payments and discounts
findings.evidence: permission `fees.refund` exists (`prisma/rbacPermissions.js:128`) but no handler uses it; `Payment` model (`schema.prisma:1427`) has no `collectedBy`, `reference`, `receiptNo`, `refundedAt`; `applyFeeDiscount` blocks discounts below paid amount ("process a refund first", `fees.js:870`) yet no refund exists. Discount apply/remove, fee delete and collections write no audit row (exams have `logExamAudit`, fees do not).
findings.impact: wrong or duplicate collections cannot be reversed in-app; no answer to "who collected or discounted this".
findings.recommendation: add `Payment.collectedById/collectedByName`, a `FeeAuditLog` model written in the same transaction, and a `POST /api/fees/payments/[id]/reverse` gated by `fees.refund`. **Effort:** M–L - Money handling: `Int` rupee columns (no floats), PERCENT discount rounded with `Math.round`, late fee computed on read (`lateFeeAmountFor`) so `payableAmount` drifts upward daily while `status` was set PAID earlier with a fixed `paidAmount` (BIZ-003 side effect); manual amounts like `10.5` would raise a Prisma Int error returned as 400 with raw message.

findings.title: Marks edits after approval/publish do not invalidate or recompute results; marks save is non-transactional
findings.evidence: `saveExamMarks` (`lib/examMarks.js:164-258`) for an admin overwrites `status` with `Draft`/`Submitted` on rows that were `Approved`/`Published` (`:247`) and does not touch `ExamResult`; results are only recomputed when an admin runs generate manually (`examResults.js:113`). Upserts run one by one without a transaction (`:240-258`), so a failure leaves a partly saved sheet. `row.studentId` is not checked against the schedule roster. Max marks are checked at save time but `updateExamSchedule` can lower `maxMarks`/`passingMarks` later with no re-validation. `generateExamResults` re-upsert resets `status` to `Draft` (`:207`), un-publishing results parents already saw.
findings.recommendation: when a mark of a published exam changes, flag the student's `ExamResult` stale (or recompute) and keep status; wrap the row loop in `$transaction`; validate studentIds against the roster. **Effort:** M

findings.title: Attendance reports key history on the student's CURRENT class/section
findings.evidence: `statusFromMap` (`lib/attendance.js:190-196`) looks up `${date}|${student.class}|${student.section}` using the student's CURRENT class/section for all historical dates; `relevantStudents` also filters on the current `academicSession`.
findings.impact: after a section change or promotion within the same session view, earlier days vanish from the student's report; a student recorded in two blobs (old and new section the same day) is counted once and silently.
findings.recommendation: join against `StudentEnrollment` for the date range or scan all `records` blobs for the studentId. **Effort:** M

findings.title: Promotion: promote and retain run as parallel transactions; no status/target validation; no fee/dues handling
findings.evidence: `app/api/students/promote/route.js` runs `promoteStudents` and `retainStudentsInSession` with `Promise.all` (separate transactions); a student id in both lists, or a conflict in one, leaves the other committed. `promoteStudents` (`lib/students.js:738`) does not require `status: 'Active'`, does not check the target class is above the source, and does nothing about unpaid fees of the old session or fee generation for the new one.
findings.recommendation: run the two operations sequentially in one transaction, filter `status: 'Active'`, call `generateFeesForNewStudent` after promotion. **Effort:** M

findings.title: Notification/push fan-out is fire-and-forget (un-awaited) on serverless; no retry or outbox
findings.evidence: `notifyNoticeRecipients` is called without `await` (`lib/notices.js:542`), as are `notifyPaymentConfirmed` (`lib/fees.js:1052`, `:1130`), `createAdminNotification`. On Vercel the function can be frozen after the response is sent. Expo errors are only logged; `DeviceNotRegistered` tokens are pruned (good); no retry; support Pusher events use public channels with ticket ids only.
findings.recommendation: use `after()`/`waitUntil` (see `node_modules/next/dist/docs` for the current API) or await inside the request. **Effort:** S

findings.title: Missing indexes: no schoolId-leading index on Payment, StudentFee, Notice, CalendarEvent; unindexed FK columns
findings.evidence: `pg_indexes` (local DB) and schema. Query patterns from `lib/*.js` vs index: - Students list/roster by `(schoolId, academicSession, class, section, status)`: `Students_schoolId_academicSession_class_section_status_idx` present. Good. Searches (`contains`, insensitive, on names/admissionId, `guardian` JSON path, `lib/students.js:268-286`) cannot use it beyond `schoolId`. - Attendance by date/class: unique `(schoolId, academicSession, date, className, sectionName)` serves day and date-range lookups. Good. Dashboard trend `WHERE schoolId` scans all rows of the school (see PERF-003). - Payments by school/status/date (`lib/fees.js:704-720`, `1408-1416`, `1537`, `1551`, `lib/dashboard.js:342`): the only indexes on `Payment` are the two `razorpay*` uniques. No `(schoolId, status, paidAt)` / `(schoolId, createdAt)` index; `Payment.studentId` and `Payment.studentFeeId` (FKs, used by ledger and fee detail) are unindexed. - StudentFee by school (`loadSchoolFees`, `lib/fees.js:1340`; groupBy at `:1413`): only `(studentId, academicSession, term)` unique exists; no `schoolId`-leading index. Local `EXPLAIN` of the payments query uses a Seq Scan (tiny table, not conclusive). - Notices (`lib/notices.js:58`), CalendarEvents (`lib/calendarEvents.js:40`), Subjects/Classes lists: filtered on `schoolId` with `orderBy createdAt/startDate`; Notice and CalendarEvent have no index at all. - Per-student lookups with no student-leading index: `ParentStudentLink(studentId)` (used by notification fan-out and fees, `lib/notices.js:477`, `lib/fees.js:996`; only `(parentAccountId, studentId)` unique exists), `ExamMark(studentId)`, `ExamResult(studentId)` (`lib/examResults.js:245`), `StudentEnrollments(classId)`, `(sectionId)`, `Sections(classTeacherId)`, `TeacherLeave(teacherId)`, `SubjectTests(teacherId, subjectId)`. - Postgres does not index FK columns automatically, so the cascades in DB-005 (delete Student) and Class/Section/Teacher deletes also seq-scan the child tables.
findings.impact: Fine at demo size. At the stated target (hundreds of thousands of payments, millions of ExamMarks, ParentNotifications growing with every notice x student) these become sequential scans shared across all tenants, plus slow deletes. Not a proven bottleneck; marked P2 because the fix is cheap and the table with highest write volume (Payment, ParentNotifications) lacks school-leading access paths.
findings.recommendation: `@@index([schoolId, status, paidAt])` and `@@index([studentId])`, `@@index([studentFeeId])` on Payment; `@@index([schoolId, academicSession])` on StudentFee; `@@index([schoolId, createdAt])` on Notice; `@@index([schoolId, startDate])` on CalendarEvent; `@@index([studentId])` on ParentStudentLink, ExamMark, ExamResult; `@@index([classId])`/`[sectionId]` on StudentEnrollment. Consider `pg_trgm` GIN indexes if student search becomes slow.

findings.title: Hard delete of a Student cascades away exam results, marks, enrollment history and the "append-only" promotion log
findings.evidence: `lib/students.js:673-698` `deleteStudent` runs `prisma.student.delete`; it only fails (P2003) if StudentFee/Payment/MonthlyReport/YearlyReport/SubjectTestMark rows exist (Restrict). `pg_constraint` (local DB) and schema show Cascade from Student to `ExamMark`, `ExamResult`, `ExamOptionalEnrollment`, `StudentEnrollment`, `StudentPromotionLog`, `ParentNotification`, `ParentStudentLink`. `schema.prisma:1036-1040` documents `StudentPromotionLog` as "append-only ... never updated/deleted". The student's id also stays inside `Attendance.records` JSON.
findings.impact: A student who has exam marks and results but no fee row (e.g. fees not generated, or a school not using the fee module) can be hard-deleted, silently deleting published results, enrollment history and the promotion log (data a school is typically required to retain). Which students are deletable depends on an unrelated module's data. No soft-delete column exists; `status` TransferredOut/Graduated is the workaround and is advisory only. All 20+ `School` relations are Restrict, so a school cannot be offboarded/purged by a single delete and there is no documented tenant export/purge procedure.
findings.recommendation: Make delete = status change (or an `archivedAt DateTime?` column) for any student with enrollments/results; restrict hard delete to students with no academic or financial history; change `StudentPromotionLog.student` and `ExamResult.student` to Restrict.

findings.title: All business dates are String; school timezone setting is never used to compute "today"
findings.evidence: `String` date columns: `Student.admissionDate`, `dob`; `Teacher.dob`, `joiningDate`, `relievingDate`; `Attendance.date`; `TeacherAttendance.date`; `Exam.startDate/endDate`; `ExamSchedule.examDate`; `FeeStructureTerm.startDate`; `AcademicSession.startDate/endDate`; `CalendarEvent.startDate/endDate`; `Notice.expiryDate`; `Homework.assignedDate`; `TeacherLeave.startDate/endDate`; `MonthlyReport.month`. Month filters use string prefixes (`lib/dashboard.js:101,109` `startsWith`), ranges rely on lexicographic order (`lib/attendance.js:174` `gte/lte` on strings). Local DB: all 163 attendance dates and 190 admission dates are well-formed 10-char values (no malformed data observed today). `lib/dateUtils.js:1-25` computes "today" from the server's local clock (`getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`), `lib/exams.js:128`, `lib/examMarks.js:413` use `toISOString().slice(0,10)` (UTC). `School.timezone` is saved (`lib/schoolSettings.js:151`) but grep finds no use of it in any date computation.
findings.impact: No DB-level validation (any string can be stored); correctness depends on every writer emitting `YYYY-MM-DD`. On Vercel the server clock is normally UTC, so for an Asia/Kolkata school between 00:00 and 05:30 local time "today" is the previous day: attendance "mark today", the 14:00 deadline (`School.attendanceDeadlineTime`, applied with server-local `setHours`), exam "upcoming/ongoing" and fee-term generation can act on the wrong day. Date arithmetic and reporting in SQL require casts.
findings.recommendation: Smallest effective step: one `schoolToday(timezone)` helper (using `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone })`) used by every "today" computation. Longer term, migrate date columns to `@db.Date` with a CHECK or a backfill migration (needs DB-001 first).

findings.title: Attendance / assignments / timetable stored as JSON arrays of ids with no FK, no per-student uniqueness, last-writer-wins saves
findings.evidence: `Attendance.records` (`schema.prisma:874`), `TeacherAttendance.records` (723), `Teacher.assignments` (661), `TimeTable.schedule` (812), `Student.guardian/feeDetails/documents` (387-400), `CalendarEvent.appliesToClasses/Sections`, `GeneratedReportJob.targetIds String[]`. `lib/attendance.js:57-69` `saveAttendance` upserts the whole `records` array supplied by the client. Local DB orphan checks (all 0): attendance record ids not in Students; teacher assignments referencing a non-existent Class; notices pointing at missing teachers. 163 attendance rows hold 1,700 student marks (about 10 per row) in the demo data.
findings.impact: (a) Student/teacher ids inside JSON are never checked by the DB: deleting or transferring a student leaves dangling ids and a student can appear twice in one `records` array. (b) Concurrency: two users saving the same class+date (teacher plus admin override) overwrite each other (last writer wins, no version/`updatedAt` precondition). (c) Per-student attendance queries cannot use an index; every report scans and `find()`s inside arrays (PERF-009). (d) The design is a conscious trade-off (documented at `schema.prisma:852-862`), reasonable for write amplification, but it makes attendance the one core record without referential integrity. `Student.feeDetails` JSON duplicates fee concepts that also live in StudentFee (see REL-005).
findings.recommendation: Keep the row-per-section shape but (1) add an `updatedAt`/version precondition to `saveAttendance`, (2) validate that every `studentId` belongs to the section's enrolled roster before saving (one query), (3) when a student is removed, either block or purge ids from records. A row-per-student `AttendanceEntry(attendanceId, studentId, status)` table is the proper fix if per-student reporting becomes a hot path; benchmark first.

findings.title: Seed script is stale against the schema and embeds plaintext demo credentials and fixed school-1 ids
findings.evidence: `prisma/seed.js:148-152` updates `Student.portalPasswordHash`, a field that no longer exists in the schema (parent logins moved to `ParentAccount`, `schema.prisma:401-403`); `prisma/seed.js:112-113` seeds two school-admin accounts with a shared plaintext demo password literal; `:148` a parent demo password literal; `:3-8,84-92` the SuperAdmin password comes from an env var or is generated and printed to stdout. Fixed ids `school-1`/`school-2` mirror `lib/school.js:5` `SEED_SCHOOL_ID`, which production code still uses as a fallback tenant (see PERF-001).
findings.impact: `npm run db:seed` will fail against the current schema (Prisma rejects an unknown field) so the documented bootstrap path for a new environment is broken. If it is patched and run in production, known demo credentials for admin and parent accounts would be created. Type only reported here; values are not repeated.
findings.recommendation: Split into `seed-reference.js` (roles, permissions, grade scale: safe for prod) and `seed-demo.js` (guarded by `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`); remove stale fields; generate random demo passwords.

findings.title: No server-side error tracking, request IDs or structured logs on the web app
findings.evidence: no Sentry/APM/logging library in `package.json`; no `instrumentation.js`; `next.config.mjs` is empty; grep for `requestId|x-request-id|correlation` in `lib`, `app`, `middleware.js` -> none. All 30 log sites are free-text `console.error('<name> failed', err)` (e.g. `lib/fees.js:567,599,1061`, `lib/pusher.js:35`, cron routes `generate-fees/route.js:21`). The mobile app does have Sentry (`schoolapp360/src/core/sentry.js:10-22`, enabled only by env flags).

findings.title: Cron endpoints fail open if CRON_SECRET is unset
findings.evidence: the check is `if (process.env.CRON_SECRET && authHeader !== ...)`, so with the variable absent the guard is skipped and anyone can GET the route. Whether production sets it was not verifiable.
findings.impact: If the variable is missing, any internet user can trigger fee generation or delete 90-day-old support tickets (idempotent-ish, but still unintended mass jobs) and obtain per-structure result JSON.
findings.recommendation: `if (!process.env.CRON_SECRET || authHeader !== \`Bearer ${process.env.CRON_SECRET}\`) return 401`.

findings.title: Cron/job failures are swallowed: HTTP 200 and no alert
findings.evidence: per-structure errors are caught and logged with `console.error` then dropped; the route still returns `{success:true, termsProcessed}` (`generate-fees/route.js:19`). Failed terms are not recorded in results, so the Vercel cron dashboard shows success. Idempotency is reasonable (`@@unique([studentId, academicSession, term])`, schema 556) so a re-run is safe.
findings.impact: A broken structure silently leaves a class unbilled; discovery is by parent complaint.
findings.recommendation: push `{structureId, term, error: err.message}` into a `failures` array, return HTTP 500 when non-empty, and notify via an alert (Sentry event or admin notification to SuperAdmin).

findings.title: Push / realtime / in-app notification failures are console-only, no retry or record
findings.evidence: `expoPush.js:41-61` handles `DeviceNotRegistered` by deleting the token (good) but logs every other ticket error and batch failure to console and returns; no receipts check (Expo's receipt API is never queried), no retry. `pusher.js:31-37` and `adminNotifications.js:38-42` swallow errors after `console.error`. In-app notification inserts are separate DB rows so they still exist when push fails.
findings.impact: Parents can miss fee/notice/homework pushes with no record visible to staff; a misconfigured Expo/FCM credential would fail every push silently until someone reads logs.
findings.recommendation: minimum: count failures per run and report them through the Sentry/log helper from OBS-001 with an alert threshold; optional later: query Expo receipts. No queue infrastructure needed.

findings.title: Most sensitive actions have no audit trail
findings.evidence: audit-style models: `ExamAuditLog` (`schema.prisma:1297`, written via `logExamAudit` from exam/mark/result/schedule libs only), `StudentPromotionLog` (1041), `MonthlyReportActivity` (1565). `ExamAuditLog` is `onDelete: Cascade` from `Exam` (line ~1302), so deleting an exam deletes its audit history. `Payment` has no recorder/actor column (`schema.prisma:1427-1443`), so a cash/UPI payment recorded by staff has no "who". No audit rows for: fee discount apply/remove, fee structure changes, payment collection, user/role creation and role change (`app/api/users/[id]/role/route.js`), password resets (admin, teacher, parent, student portal), student/teacher create-update-delete, bulk import, academic session activation, school settings and branding changes, SuperAdmin "step into school" (`schools/[id]/manage/route.js`), login success/failure, data views of Aadhaar fields.
findings.impact: Cannot answer "who changed this fee / role / record" after an incident or dispute; no evidence trail for fraud investigation or for responding to a privacy request.
findings.recommendation: one generic `AuditLog` model (`schoolId, actorId, actorRole, action, entityType, entityId, meta Json, createdAt`) and a 10-line `logAudit()` helper (same pattern as `lib/examAuditLog.js`), called from the high-value mutation points first: payments/discounts, role changes, password resets, student/teacher delete, settings. Add `recordedBy` to `Payment`. Remove cascade on ExamAuditLog or copy before delete.

findings.title: No backup/restore or incident-response documentation
findings.evidence: `docs/` contains only `API-Spec.md`; `README.md` and `docs/` grep for backup/restore/incident/runbook/disaster -> no matches. Database provider backup settings (Supabase) are outside the repo and were not accessible.

A student with any fee/payment row cannot be deleted at all (Restrict, `:686-690`); the suggested alternative is status change, which keeps all personal data. No teacher delete route exists (`app/api/teachers/[id]` has `assignments`, `reset-password`, `status`, `route.js` with PUT only). Only support tickets have a retention job (`lib/support.js:234-254`, 90 days). No data-export (access) function and no anonymisation function were found.
findings.impact: Personal data of children and staff persists indefinitely, and orphaned identity documents remain publicly reachable (PRV-002) even after a "delete". If the operator must honour deletion/withdrawal requests, there is no supported way to do it.
findings.recommendation: On delete/transfer-out purge document objects (`documents.*Url`, `aadhaarDocumentUrl`, guardian document URLs) via `deleteObject`; add an `anonymizeStudent` that blanks identifiers but keeps fee/payment rows; define a retention schedule with the school (fee records often have statutory retention — verify).

findings.title: No privacy notice, terms or consent capture anywhere (web and mobile)

Login pages, parent account creation (`lib/parentAccounts.js`) and student admission forms carry no notice or consent record; there is no consent field in `schema.prisma`.
findings.impact: The product processes data of minors (DOB, Aadhaar, caste, religion, blood group, guardian contacts). Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, personal data of persons under 18 generally requires verifiable parental/guardian consent and a notice; tracking/behavioural monitoring of children is restricted. Whether the school (data fiduciary) or SchoolApp360 (processor) must collect that here, and in what form, is a legal question; code alone shows no mechanism. Not a compliance conclusion. Mobile stores crash data via Sentry (see PRV-006); no ad/behavioural analytics SDKs were found in either `package.json`.
findings.recommendation: After legal advice: publish privacy notice/terms pages, link from login screens and app stores, add a recorded acceptance (timestamp, version) at parent first-login and a school-level data-processing agreement. Data minimisation: make caste/religion/Aadhaar optional per school.

findings.title: Money design: whole-rupee Int, derived payable amount, no DB invariants, hard-coded INR/paise

No CHECK that `paidAmount <= payable` or `amount > 0`; no receipt number or refund/reversal row type (`PaymentStatus` has no REFUNDED); abandoned Razorpay orders stay PENDING forever (local DB: 9 PENDING vs 4 SUCCESS Razorpay payments).
findings.impact: Whole rupees are acceptable for Indian school fees but cannot represent paise-level concessions; the stored `status` (PAID) can become inconsistent with a later-changing computed payable amount; no audit-grade receipt sequence per school. Not a correctness bug today.
findings.recommendation: Add CHECK constraints (`paidAmount >= 0`, `amount > 0`); add a per-school receipt number on SUCCESS payments; freeze late fee into the StudentFee (or record it as a StudentFeeItem) when applied; add a PENDING-order expiry job. Keep Int but document the unit as rupees.

ON "AcademicSessions"("schoolId") WHERE status = 'Active'`; `ON "Sections"("classTeacherId","academicSession") WHERE "classTeacherId" IS NOT NULL`; `ON "User"(lower(email)) WHERE "schoolId" IS NULL`. findings.title: Third-party processors and hosting region need a documented basis
findings.evidence: data sent (code-read): Expo push — device token, title, body such as the payment amount, and `data:{type,studentId}` (`lib/fees.js:1006-1012`); notice/homework/exam pushes similar. Pusher — IDs and status only (`lib/support.js:146,180-182,212`), no names or message text. SMTP — teacher invite/reset link emails (`lib/teachers.js:45`, `lib/emailTemplates.js:19+`). Razorpay — fee amount/order data. R2 — photos, identity documents, notice PDFs, support attachments. Mobile Sentry — crash/perf traces (`sendDefaultPii` is not set). `vercel.json:2` pins region `syd1`; the prior audit noted a Supabase Sydney database.
findings.impact: Indian students' data is processed on infrastructure outside India and by several processors; whether that is permitted and what contracts/notices are required is a legal question (DPDP cross-border rules depend on government notifications). Not concluded here.
findings.recommendation: maintain a short processor/region table in the privacy notice and DPA; confirm R2 jurisdiction and Supabase region; consider India-region hosting if legal advice requires.

findings.title: Unredacted error objects logged; token logged in push errors
findings.evidence: `lib/expoPush.js:53-55` logs the recipient Expo push token (a device identifier) on every ticket error; many sites pass the whole `err` object (`lib/fees.js:567,599,1061`, `lib/notices.js:523`, `lib/parentNotifications.js:37`). Prisma error objects can embed query arguments. I did not find a site that logs request bodies, passwords, OTPs or Aadhaar values directly. No redaction layer exists.
findings.impact: Low today; becomes a PII/identifier leak into log storage if a failing query includes student fields.
findings.recommendation: log `err.code`/`err.message` via the helper from OBS-001, drop the token from line 53-55 (log batch index only).

findings.title: Student placement has two sources of truth (strings on Student and StudentEnrollment FKs)

findings.title: nodemailer 10.0.1 has multiple advisories (DoS, cross-transport TLS servername reuse); sharp has libheif/librsvg advisories
findings.evidence: npm audit --json: nodemailer <=10.0.8, sharp <=0.35.5-rc.1; lib/email.js:11-26 builds one transport from env
findings.impact: Recipient parsing DoS reachable via user-supplied emails; the cross-tenant SMTP issue does not apply while a single env-configured transport is used.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade nodemailer and sharp to fixed versions.

findings.title: Set-password link: no server-side password policy, 7-day plaintext token, no redemption throttling, no status re-check; reset only exists for teachers
findings.evidence: lib/teachers.js:7,458-470,507-524 (no length check at redemption, status not re-checked); prisma/schema.prisma:131-132,666-667 (passwordSetToken stored unhashed)
findings.impact: A DB or log leak exposes usable reset tokens for a week; weak passwords can be set through the link; parents and admins have no self-service reset.
findings.recommendation: Store a hash of the token, shorten TTL to 1-2 hours, enforce min length and common-password checks server-side, rate-limit redemption.

findings.title: Login rate limiter is bypassable and enables targeted lockout: client-controlled x-forwarded-for first hop, per-instance memory, 8-attempt per-account counter
findings.evidence: lib/auth/loginRateLimit.js:19-21,51-55,61-71; no limit on lib/parentAccounts.js change-password current-password guesses
findings.impact: Attackers rotate XFF to defeat the IP bucket and cold starts reset counters; anyone can lock a victim account out for 15 minutes per instance.
findings.recommendation: Shared store (Upstash/Postgres), use platform-provided client IP, add progressive delay rather than hard lockout.

findings.title: Cross-tenant reference gaps: section update not tied to class, classTeacherId and marks studentId not validated against the school
findings.evidence: lib/classes.js:444-449 (section updated by id after checking only the class), 401-420,491-520 (classTeacherId unvalidated); lib/examMarks.js:243-247 (rows[].studentId unvalidated)
findings.impact: With a foreign cuid a caller can mutate another tenant's section status or link foreign teachers/students into own records; needs a guessed id so likelihood is low.
findings.recommendation: Scope every update by schoolId in the where clause (updateMany with schoolId) and validate referenced ids belong to the school.

findings.title: Login lookups by email are global while uniqueness is per school or absent, so same-email accounts collide
findings.evidence: lib/teachers.js:437-440 (Teacher.loginEmail not unique); lib/parentAccounts.js:108-111 with prisma/schema.prisma:285 (@@unique schoolId+email); lib/rbac.js:45-48
findings.impact: A parent or staff member with the same email in two schools may be unable to sign in or land in the wrong tenant.
findings.recommendation: Make login emails globally unique or require a school code at login.

findings.title: Push token registration transfers ownership of an existing token to the caller
findings.evidence: lib/pushTokens.js:8-13 (upsert by token updates owner); app/api/notifications/register-token/route.js:12-36
findings.impact: A caller who learns another device token can redirect that device's notifications to their own identity; also tokens are not removed on logout (MOB-004).
findings.recommendation: Refuse re-binding of a token owned by another user unless proven by device; delete token on logout.
